notes:
CIRCUIT: a simple two-node ladder. I-DC #2 (11A, arrow up), R#1 (10ohm) and the left plate of C#0 (9uF) all hang between the upper-left rail and the bottom rail; the right plate of C#0, L#3 (9mH) and V-DC #4 (60V, '+' up / '-' down) all hang between the upper-right rail and the bottom rail. The single bottom rail carries GND #5. So C#0 is the only element bridging the two upper nodes. The heavy rectangle around the page is a drawing frame, not a wire; the tracer correctly excluded it.

NET MAP
  0  = the bottom rail, y~545..560, running from (272,545) under the current source all the way east to (838,550) under the voltage source: bottom of I-DC #2, bottom of R#1, bottom of L#3, bottom of V-DC #4, and the GND #5 stem dropping at (558,556). 5 terminals.
  n1 = the upper-LEFT rail at y~372, from the top of I-DC #2 at (275,407)->(272,372) east to the left plate of C#0 at (533,370), with R#1's top stub joining at S3 (414,370). Terminals: 2.0, 1.0, 0.0.
  n2 = the upper-RIGHT rail at y~375, from the right plate of C#0 at (604,377) east to (838,372) and down to the top of V-DC #4, with L#3's top stub joining at S5 (688,378). Terminals: 0.1, 3.0, 4.0.

JUDGEMENT CALLS / SITES - all four CRITICAL sites are unambiguous T shapes, no dot and no hop needed, and each was confirmed on its 5x crop:
  * S3 (414,370) JUNCTION - R#1's top lead rises and terminates on the upper-left rail, which runs straight through east-west. The crop shows a slight ink thickening right at the meeting point (dot score 1.8), consistent with a deliberate node. The other reading is not even expressible here: there is no wire above the rail at this x, so 'crossing' would strand R#1's top terminal on a 1-terminal net.
  * S5 (688,378) JUNCTION - identical shape for L#3's top lead onto the upper-right rail. Same argument.
  * S11 (416,545) JUNCTION - R#1's bottom lead descends and terminates on the bottom rail. Same argument (nothing below the rail here).
  * S14 (699,560) JUNCTION - L#3's bottom lead descends and terminates on the bottom rail. Same argument.
  In every one of these four the 'crossing' reading would leave one element with a dangling terminal and no return path, so electrical impossibility settles them even before the ink evidence.
  * Non-critical sites left at default: S0 (564,329) and S2 (597,331) are strokes of the handwritten '9uF' above the capacitor; S8 (220,457) is the 'A' of '11A' brushing the current-source box; S10 (730,483) is the '9mH' label brushing the inductor box. None touches the netlist.

PORTS: no fixes needed. Verified every component in the comps montage - #0 p0 left / p1 right (p2,p3 are '9uF' ink), #1 p1 top / p0 bottom, #2 p1 top / p0 bottom (p2 is the 'A' glyph), #3 p0 top / p1 bottom (p2,p3,p4 are '9mH' ink), #4 p0 top / p1 bottom, #5 GND p0 stem. No 3-terminal parts on this sheet, so no pin-order risk.

CLASSES: all correct. #2 is a current source (circle with a vertical arrow, '11A'); #4 is a voltage source (circle with '+' over '-', '60V'); #1 is a zig-zag resistor, #3 a coil inductor, #0 a two-plate capacitor.
UNRESOLVED: none. The tracer's default assignment was already right; I made no override, only explicit confirmations. ERC clean, 6 components, 3 nets.
